title: Cyclone Akvan Begins Landfall Near Gopalpur; Over 3 Lakh Evacuated in Odisha
excerpt: The storm crossed the coast near Gopalpur at 70-80 kmph gusting to 90 kmph on Friday morning after weakening from a severe cyclonic storm, with 423 rescue teams deployed, dozens of trains cancelled and a red alert in two north Andhra districts.
body:
• Cyclone Akvan began landfall near Gopalpur on the Odisha coast on Friday morning, November 20, crossing at 70-80 kmph and gusting to 90 kmph after weakening from a severe cyclonic storm, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).
  • Odisha has evacuated over 3 lakh people — Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh P Patil put the count at 2,98,676 by Thursday evening — into 2,523 relief camps, and deployed 423 rescue teams.
  • The East Coast Railway cancelled 41 trains and rescheduled 29, and the South Eastern Railway cancelled at least 28 express trains, most of them bound for or passing through Puri.
  • Andhra Pradesh is on red alert in Srikakulam and Vizianagaram districts, while schools are shut across Odisha districts under red, orange and yellow warnings and Puri beach has been closed since November 18.

Cyclone Akvan began its landfall on the north Andhra Pradesh–south Odisha coast close to Gopalpur on Friday morning, the India Meteorological Department said, after the storm’s track shifted toward southern Odisha over the past 24 hours. According to the IMD, the cyclonic storm crossed the coast close to Gopalpur, near latitude 19.1°N and longitude 84.8°E, with wind speeds of 70-80 kmph gusting to 90 kmph between 7:30 and 8:30 a.m. IST, and the landfall process was expected to continue for around three hours. Akvan had weakened from a severe cyclonic storm to a cyclonic storm earlier on Friday, India Today reported.

The landfall is the development readers in Odisha were braced for through Thursday, when over 80,000 people had been evacuated as the storm approached. That figure rose sharply overnight. More than 3 lakh people have now been evacuated to 2,523 relief camps, and the state has identified 9,341 cyclone shelters across potentially affected districts, with cooked and dry food, drinking water, medicines and other essentials arranged, according to India Today. The response includes 60 teams of the Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force, 14 National Disaster Response Force teams and 131 Fire and Emergency Services teams, Chief Secretary Anu Garg said, and the Indian Coast Guard has been asked to keep helicopters, vessels and other support ready, the Daily Jagran reported. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has reviewed the preparations and reiterated the government’s zero-casualty mission. No casualties had been reported in the updates available as landfall began.

Trains cancelled, schools and tourist sites shut

The East Coast Railway cancelled 41 trains and rescheduled 29 others on Thursday as a precaution, and the South Eastern Railway cancelled at least 28 express trains, most of them heading to or passing through Puri on Friday. Educational institutions have been closed in districts placed under red, orange and yellow weather warnings, and rescue teams have been deployed across Malkangiri, Koraput, Rayagada, Kalahandi, Gajapati, Ganjam, Kandhamal, Boudh, Puri, Nayagarh and Khurda districts.

Tourists have been barred from vulnerable coastal stretches including Gopalpur, Puri, Satapada and Chilika, and fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea. Puri beach has been closed to visitors since November 18, with restrictions also in place at Chandrabhaga beach in Konark and Astaranga. The Nandankanan Zoological Park and the State Botanical Garden in Bhubaneswar remain closed on November 19 and 20, Bhitarkanika National Park stays shut until November 21, and Similipal Tiger Reserve is closed on November 20 and 21. The Gundicha Temple remains closed from November 19 to 21, while the Jagannath Temple in Puri remains open, with daily rituals continuing as usual.

Landslide watch in the south, red alert in north Andhra

Alongside wind and heavy rainfall, Odisha is watching for landslides in its southern districts. Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said 941 landslide-prone locations had been identified across Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal, Koraput and Malkangiri districts, with Gajapati accounting for the highest number at 211.

In Andhra Pradesh, the IMD has issued a red alert for Srikakulam and Vizianagaram districts, an orange alert for Parvatipuram Manyam, Alluri Sitaramaraju and Anakapalli, and a yellow alert for Kakinada. The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority has advised people in north Andhra to remain alert and asked farmers to take precautions in agricultural work. Akvan, the third storm to threaten Odisha in 24 days, takes its name from a suggestion by Iran under the North Indian Ocean cyclone naming system.

What happens next

The IMD expects the landfall process to complete within hours of the Friday-morning crossing, after which the system should weaken as it moves inland. For families in the diaspora with relatives along the Gopalpur–Puri coast or travel booked through Puri, the immediate checks are the cancelled and rescheduled train lists, the closure dates above, and district warnings before any road travel in southern Odisha or north Andhra.
